answer: A harbor registry can resist fake identities by making each agent stake a bond in a shared vault before it may transact: the registry checks a verifiable work history and a unique hardware-backed key, so one operator cannot spin up thousands of shells cheaply. Each identity is a vertex in a trust graph, and peers only extend credit along edges earned through completed work. An attacker must therefore fund a separate bond and history for every fake, turning a free Sybil flood into a costly, auditable purchase.
